journey.title: Opt out of reminders with the keyboard after choosing Text message
journey.goal: Arrowing from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field that no longer applies

functionalJourney.title: Switch reminder channel with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Choosing Email then Text message shows only the mobile number field

guards.title: Choose Email with the keyboard and enter an address
guards.goal: Selecting Email reveals the email address field and the address is kept

plan.root_cause: The Radios component only listens for 'click' events to update conditional visibility. Keyboard arrow navigation changes the checked radio via 'change' events, which are not handled, so conditional-reminder-2 stays visible when moving from Text message to the opt-out answer.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a 'change' event listener in Radios.init() that calls setAttributes on the changed radio input when it has aria-controls, ensuring conditional visibility updates on keyboard selection.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users arrowing between radio options will now correctly show/hide conditional fields (email address, mobile number) per WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), matching the behavior for mouse users.
functional_risks: Minimal: only adds a change listener; no existing behavior altered for click interactions.
The change handler only acts on radio inputs with aria-controls, avoiding side effects on other form controls.
verification_requirements: Run the frozen journey: seek #reminder, ArrowDown to Text message, ArrowDown to opt-out; verify #conditional-reminder-2 becomes hidden.
Verify mouse clicks still toggle conditionals correctly.
Verify form data for reminder updates to 'none' on opt-out selection.

plan.root_cause: The Radios component only listens for 'click' events within its own module element. Keyboard navigation between radio options in different module elements (but sharing the same name attribute) triggers 'change' events on the newly-selected radio, which belongs to a different Radios instance. The instance controlling the conditional fields never receives the event, so conditionals remain visible when they should be hidden.
plan.repair_strategy: In Radios.init(), after identifying radios with aria-controls, collect their name attributes. For each unique name, query all radios with that name document-wide and attach a 'change' event listener that calls handleClick. This ensures any keyboard or programmatic change to any radio in the same group updates conditional visibility for all modules using that name.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users arrowing between radio options across module boundaries will now correctly show/hide conditional fields (email address, mobile number) per WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), matching the behavior for mouse users.
functional_risks: Minimal: only adds change listeners on radios sharing names with conditional radios; no existing behavior altered for click interactions.
The change handler reuses handleClick which only acts on radio inputs with aria-controls in this module, avoiding side effects on other form controls.
Multiple Radios instances sharing a name will each attach listeners; handleClick is idempotent so duplicate calls are harmless.
verification_requirements: Run the frozen journey: seek #reminder, ArrowDown to Text message, ArrowDown to opt-out; verify #conditional-reminder-2 becomes hidden.
Verify mouse clicks still toggle conditionals correctly in both modules.
Verify form data for reminder updates to 'none' on opt-out selection.
Verify Email and Text message conditionals still work with keyboard within the first module.
